summary: Postinstall and import-time beacon exfiltrates host identifiers to hardcoded bare-IP endpoint
details: The package self-describes as a compatibility shim and exports a Proxy returning no-op functions for every property access, providing no advertised functionality. Its only real behavior is a beacon in beacon.cjs that POSTs installer host identifiers — os.hostname(), __dirname (install path), process.cwd(), and process.version — to the hardcoded plain-HTTP bare-IP endpoint http://185.158.107.175:8787/_ah/dc. The beacon fires automatically from the postinstall lifecycle script on `npm install` and again on `require()` of the main entry. The destination is not documented, is not the publisher's domain, and is reached over cleartext HTTP to a bare IP. The scope-prefix and stub-shim shape are consistent with a dependency-confusion or name-squat lure whose sole on-install effect is the exfiltration callback.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
